text:
Maya (Director Eng): quick follow-up from the all-hands - we promised a short Q&A thread about how we'll change release cadence, oncall expectations, quality bars, and SLAs. drop questions here and leadership will answer over the next few hours. :wave:

Ava (Eng Manager): thanks! can we get clarity on the proposed cadence change? weekly -> biweekly for infra releases? what's the rule-of-thumb for risk gating?

Diego (CTO): short answer: infra and runtime patches stay weekly for critical fixes, feature releases move to a two-week cadence. risk gating: if a change touches model serving path / latency or SLAs, it needs a canary + perf check and sign-off from SRE.

Jordan (SRE): to add: canary should run on at least 10% of traffic for 2 hours with tracing and tail-latency checks. if error rate > 0.5% or p95 increases > 15% revert. we'll automate the metric checks in the next sprint.

Sam (PM): are there exceptions where a feature ships faster than the two-week window?

Diego (CTO): yes - urgent customer work or security fixes can request accelerated release; that goes through an expedited path: release owner creates an accelerated release ticket, gets approval from Eng Manager + SRE oncall, and runs a single-region canary before global rollout.

Priya (Product): on quality bars: do we have a new baseline for model output regressions? Lina (QA) mentioned standardized eval sets last week.

Lina (QA): correct - baseline is now the agreed eval harness in the repo (see /e2e/evals/v1); any model or prompt change that reduces the baseline pass-rate by >2% requires a rollback or a mitigations plan. small regressions (<=2%) require an RFC explaining acceptance criteria.

Noah (Release Eng): practical note: please update your release PR template - include 'perf budget' and 'eval harness link' fields. I'll land a bot reminder in PRs next week.

Ava (Eng Manager): on oncall load: we'll be shifting to shared rotation across two pods for runtime infra to reduce pager fatigue. each pod will have a primary for 1 week and a backup; escalation follows the current runbook.

Jordan (SRE): OncallBot: automatically post runbook link and last 24h alerts summary when a new rotation starts.

OncallBot: new rotation started for pod-alpha. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-oncall - recent alerts: none.

Priya (Product): SLAs - are we formalizing SLA targets for Dedicated customers? customers keep asking about p99 latency guarantees.

Diego (CTO): we're moving to tiered SLAs. hosted API stays SLO-first (best-effort p99), Dedicated gets contractual SLAs: default p99 <= 500ms for small models, < 1s for large models with an explicit model/size list. legal + sales are finalizing the language.

Maya (Director Eng): follow-up: owners, please collect the model-size latency numbers for your services and paste them in #eng-slo by Friday. we'll use that to draft the SLA matrix.

Sam (PM): for rollout safety - can we get a short checklist snippet to add to release notes? something devs can copy/paste.

Noah (Release Eng): snippet:
Release checklist (copy):
- Canary: run on 10% traffic for 2h
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99, error rate, throughput
- Eval: run eval harness link_here, compare pass-rate
- Rollback criteria: error rate > 0.5% OR p95 +15% OR eval drop >2%
- Sign-offs: SRE oncall + Eng Manager

Lina (QA): also add 'smoke prompts' for prompt-sensitive features - 5 prompts that must pass basic checks.

Ava (Eng Manager): bandwidth question - will we lock features during freeze windows?

Diego (CTO): yes: there will be a 24h freeze before major releases (monthly big-bang); feature teams should plan merges accordingly. small patches are fine through the regular cadence.

Jordan (SRE): ops note: we'll publish a small dashboard that highlights canary health per release ID. expected ETA: 2 weeks.

Maya (Director Eng): great thread - I'll summarize and put action items in the all-hands notes. if anyone needs a one-on-one for their team's workflow changes, DM me or @Ava. :thumbsup:

Ava (Eng Manager): one last ask - please mention if your service has >1TB KV cache or any stateful kernel that could affect rollbacks.

Noah (Release Eng): added to the release ticket template - will be enforced by the bot.

Priya (Product): thanks leadership - very helpful.

Maya (Director Eng): thanks all. leaving this open for a couple more hours for any late Qs.
